fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker! Moses, Israel's leader, and Aaron walk up to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, with a message. They say the LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.” (Exodus 5:1) A feast, for the LORD. Now THAT is an invitation. Pharaoh gets handed the best one ever and doesn't even RSVP.

I see why you'd go there, friend, but nobody mentions a permanent move in this message. Moses and Aaron tell Pharaoh the LORD, the God of Israel, says, “Let My people go, so that they may hold a feast to Me in the wilderness.” (Exodus 5:1) The ask is a feast to the LORD. Packing up for good isn't on the invitation. That's like showing up with a suitcase when all you were asked to bring was a dish.

The wilderness is where Moses and Aaron asked to go for the feast, but this verse sends the people somewhere else. “So the people scattered all over the land of Egypt to gather stubble for straw.” (Exodus 5:12) The text puts the search all over Egypt. I think this part of the story is heavy, because the work just got harder for them.

problems.problem: The explanation ends with a pleasant but generic comment rather than Papa Dorin's distinctive voice.
The explanation is clear but flat and generic, with little of Papa Dorin's personality.
Calling the people's forced search for straw an exhausting scavenger hunt makes light of their suffering under Pharaoh's harsher labor demands.
